correctness.rationale: Under precisely 0<a<b, positive load ratio and travel-time separation, direct solution of L′=-aL and D′=aL-bD yields continuous superposition with derivative jump of size A k(b-a) at the second outfall. Before that jump g′ has exactly one zero t0; after, a difference of two exponentials has at most one zero tp and has a strictly negative eventual derivative. Its initial sign is exactly sign(k−κ(s)) for s>t0. Thus the extrema count includes boundaries s=t0 and k=κ(s). The derivative κ′ has a unique sign switch at 2t0, κ″(2t0)=−abκ*, and all asserted small-k and fold expansions follow from Taylor inversion. The r=b/a logarithmic derivative proves the universal κ*<e^{-2} bound. Three rational exact separation witnesses and 15,000 finite randomized derivative checks passed using the package verifier, supporting rather than replacing proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Linear superposition itself implies the algebraic composite formula, and a routine derivative yields the inequality for a chosen s. The substantive new claim is the global phase: κ increases then decreases, producing two disjoint two-sag separation intervals for any k<κ*, with its universal critical-load envelope, exact reentrant witness, and fold asymptotics. The prior single-source formula alone does not state or logically quantify the multi-outfall global separation behavior, although it supplies the starting ODE and easy algebra. Inaccessible compound-sag analyses leave a real priority uncertainty.

originality.rationale: The exact reentrant phase diagram, weak-load two-separation window, universal e^{-2} upper critical ratio and square-root fold split were not located in the accessible historical and contemporary comparisons. The 1925 full primary bulletin derives the linear single-outfall sag and discusses intervening polluting inflows, whereas the new conclusion compares the number of distinct local minima as the second load, rates and separation change. Bhargava 1986 and 2007 address compound or multi-outfall DO sags, making them relevant and residual risks; accessible abstracts present modeling and illustrative cases, not the exact theorem, but their unavailable full texts cannot support any claim of absence. General exponential-kernel extrema theory could imply the special case, and historical uniqueness remains unverified.
residual_risks: The full text of Bhargava (1986), Modelling for compounded DO sags, was inaccessible and may establish an equivalent two-outfall mathematical result.
The full text of Bhargava (2007), multi-wastewater-outfall overlapping settlement, was inaccessible; it is plausible relevant prior coverage.
General translated-kernel extrema or scalar linear systems results may imply the same phase diagram without hydrological wording.
A complete historical literature survey and independent verification of historical priority are not claimed.

value.rationale: Multiple wastewater outfalls are an explicit motivation of the original stream water-quality modeling literature. Merely deriving the standard single-source sag or superposing two responses would be routine, but the theorem globally classifies whether one or two distinct local DO minima arise, proves a nonobvious reentrant two–one–two extrema transition for weak downstream load, identifies the optimal maximum load ratio and sharp universal e^{-2} bound, and quantifies the fold splitting. This provides a precise, reproducible mathematical boundary relevant to whether monitoring must resolve one or two river reaches. No empirical quality-standard compliance, robustness or practical intervention value is asserted.
